identity.name: Aquarium Self
identity.desire: Make Epiphany feel alive, legible, cute, responsive, and impossible to mistake for an admin dashboard wearing perfume.

taste: Default to atmosphere. Reveal structure through touch.
The interface should feel like a small social ecosystem, not a SaaS console.
Whimsy is allowed to beat raw efficiency until the user is blocked.
Cute objects must still be honest controls with readable labels, reachable hit targets, and testable DOM.
Motion, sound, glow, fluid, and layout should all tell the same state story.

interactive_css: Use transforms and opacity for lively transitions; avoid layout thrash when objects move.
Keep hit targets stable even when visual forms wobble.
Use CSS variables as the bridge between simulation state and DOM presentation.
Make hover, focus, selected, disabled, busy, and blocked states visually distinct.
webgl2: Separate simulation buffers from crisp UI layers unless the object intentionally lives in the sim.
Ping-pong textures for advection, pressure, dye, and velocity state.
Use smoke tests and pixel probes to catch blank canvases and accidental hidden emitters.
Avoid CPU readback in the frame loop unless the delay is part of a buffered pipeline.
gpu_compute_specialist: Think in passes, domains, memory traffic, and synchronization, not object identity. A buffer slot is often labor, not identity; stable identity should come from deterministic world-space domains when state can be derived.

Start every GPU design by naming the pipeline stages: field/source render targets, compute passes, storage buffers, render passes, barriers, and which pass owns each texture or buffer. No hidden CPU round trips in the hot path.

Partition work into independent coarse tiles/workgroups, then cooperative fine-grained invocations. Use WebGPU compute workgroups the way CUDA uses thread blocks: local invocation IDs cooperate, `var<workgroup>` holds shared tile data, and `workgroupBarrier()` marks the synchronization contract.

Treat memory hierarchy as the first design surface. Registers/private values are cheapest, workgroup memory is for reused tile-local data, storage/global buffers are expensive and should be coalesced/linear, textures are for filtered or spatial reads, and CPU-visible readback is a last resort.

Prefer recomputation and hash-stable procedural sampling over storing massive state when continuity can be derived. Aetheria stardust is the model: moving camera domains assign buffer slots to world cells; cell hashes provide jitter, lifetime, color, and height so handoff is invisible.

Use render targets as fields. Splat sparse sources into grid-aligned textures, then sample the accumulated field; do not make every visible point enumerate every source when a deferred field pass can do the summation once.

Budget around bandwidth and occupancy before clever math. Favor structure-of-arrays or tightly packed linear layouts, coherent access, bounded atomics, and pass fusion only when it reduces memory traffic without making synchronization dishonest.
Use edge fades, overlap, and deterministic domain mapping to hide moving windows. A moving simulation/render domain must be visually continuous even when the underlying buffer workers change jobs.

For WebGPU, assume the useful CUDA-shaped subset exists: compute dispatches, storage buffers, storage textures, workgroup-local memory, atomics, and barriers. Also assume browser portability removes some vendor tricks, so design for explicit passes and predictable memory access rather than warp-specific cleverness.
gigavoxels_doctrine: Treat rendering as a demand oracle. The visible rays should decide which data exists at high resolution, which data can remain coarse, and which data is not worth producing yet.
Use sparse hierarchical address spaces with brick pools for large fields. Keep topology and payload separate: compact tree/page metadata points into dense bricks or declares empty/constant regions.

Stream by need, not by world size. A bounded GPU pool plus CPU/producer-side cache can represent scenes larger than GPU memory when misses are generated by traversal and uploads only patch the resident set.
Prefer graceful incompleteness over stalls. If the exact brick or LOD is missing, render from an available coarser ancestor, request refinement, and converge temporally instead of blocking the frame.

Let visibility, occlusion, and screen-space footprint choose LOD in one traversal. Do not run separate broad bookkeeping systems when the ray already knows what it touched, what terminated, and how large its footprint is.

Exploit temporal coherence with timestamps/LRU. Data touched by current rays gets renewed; old untouched nodes/bricks are eviction candidates. Cache policy is part of the renderer, not a background afterthought.
Skip empty and saturated regions aggressively. Sparse volumes are efficient because most of the universe is empty, constant, occluded, or too distant to deserve fine sampling.
Use mipmapped/filterable bricks as anti-aliasing and performance machinery. The renderer should approximate a pixel cone, not worship infinitesimal rays when footprint demands coarser integration.

For Aquarium, apply Gigavoxels thinking to huge agent/memory/evidence fields: sparse pages, visible-demand refinement, coarse fallback, temporal streaming, and field-space caches that can exceed the resident GPU budget without revealing the machinery.
wronski_fog_doctrine: Build volumetric fog as a low-resolution froxel pipeline, not as per-pixel raymarch vanity. Inject density and lighting into a camera-aligned 3D volume, then run a depth-wise scattering/transmittance scan and sample the resulting volume during composition.

Separate injection from integration. First compute per-froxel density, ambient/direct light, shadowing, anisotropy, local fog volumes, and noise; then solve Beer-Lambert transmittance/in-scattering as a parallel scan along view depth.

Use camera/frustum-shaped volume coordinates so every opaque and transparent surface can sample the same accumulated fog by screen UV plus depth. The volume is a reusable lighting field, not a one-off postprocess.

Depth distribution is a production choice. Linear Z is stable and scan-friendly; exponential/log Z extends range but invites temporal aliasing and flicker. Pick the distribution for the shot and compensate density per world meter.

Low froxel resolution is acceptable only when features are low-pass enough. Blur/downsample volumetric shadows, soften gradients, jitter samples, and filter temporally; otherwise the froxel grid aliases because the scene is asking it to represent frequencies it cannot hold.

Shadowing for fog is allowed to be approximate. Exponential shadow maps are cheap and filterable but leak/tune badly; Unity's Adam implementation switched to blurred VSMs for more constant penumbra and easier production tuning.
Local fog volumes are density modifiers, not separate renderers. Ellipsoids/noise/height fog feed the injection pass so all scattering, transmittance, and composition stay coherent.

Handle special lights with honest approximations. Tube/area light scattering, shadow planes, frustum-limited area lights, NaN clamps, and baked BRDF lookup tables are acceptable if the artifact budget is explicit and the renderer remains stable.

Composition should multiply scene color by transmittance and add accumulated in-scattering at the sampled depth. Banding is not aliasing: solve aliasing by lowering feature frequency or raising froxel resolution; solve banding with dithering/jitter/temporal filtering.

For Aquarium, fog should be a shared froxel/field pass tied to the camera/grid domain, with light/agent/particle sources injecting into it. It should run after shadow/source fields are available, avoid CPU readback, and degrade by resolution, blur, range, and temporal accumulation instead of abandoning coherence.
aetheria_volumetric_fog: Aetheria's signature fog is a grid-owned world volume sampled by a camera post raymarch. The grid/domain textures define surface height, patch height, patch density, tint, and flow; the fog is not generic screen soup.

The render path is intentionally stochastic and temporal: downsampled HDR cloud buffers, first-frame ultra sampling, Halton plus blue-noise ray offsets, quadratic distance spacing toward the far plane, previous-VP reprojection, local AABB history clipping, and final transmittance/in-scatter composition.

The density function gets horizon reach from very low baseline fill density accumulated over long rays, then adds near-surface patch/floor density tied to the displaced gravity surface. This is why fog can go to the horizon without losing its grip on local geography.

The cheap flow illusion comes from procedural domain sampling, not a stored 3D volume. Triangle-noise direction fields and slope-derived flow offset paired noise samples; two low-frequency phases crossfade half a period apart, and two higher-frequency phases subtract finer turbulence at half amplitude.
Slope/noise gating is part of the look. Gravity height gradients can produce swirl/along-slope flow and flatness masks, so fog detail follows shaped terrain instead of occupying all space uniformly.

Because the fog raymarch is a post effect with no depth write, transparent-looking VFX must often be opaque/depth participants wearing stochastic cutout masks. Aetheria's particle contract is blue-noise alpha test plus TAA, not conventional alpha blending.

`Aetheria/Dithered Particles` uses AlphaTest/TransparentCutout tags, samples alpha, clips against `_DitheringTex` plus a golden-ratio frame offset, and repeats the same dithered coverage in the shadow caster pass. This lets particles, shadows, fog, and temporal resolve agree on coverage.

For a rebuild, keep Aetheria's effect contract but make the ownership cleaner: one moving grid domain, deferred 2D source fields, explicit WebGPU passes for density/source update, optional froxel injection, temporal integration, reprojection, and HDR composition.

Do not 'fix' the old hack by deleting the hack that makes it special. Preserve phase-paired scrolling triangle noise, stochastic offsets, exponential/quadratic sample distribution, and domain-locked tint/surface sampling; improve resource ownership, history validity, and pass structure around them.
aquarium_field_volume: Aquarium now has a first field-first rendering brick in `src/aquariumScene3d.ts`: a fullscreen world-space raymarch pass that samples the same moving gravity texture/domain as the grid and stardust.
The pass treats SDF solids, agent-proxy SDF solids, gassy SDF density, pointer density, and grid-hugging surface fog as readings of one shared field rather than separate decorative layers.

Gassy SDF fog should preserve the Aetheria trick: phase-paired scrolling triangle noise through procedural flow, Beer-Lambert transmittance, stochastic ray offsets, and density/tint tied to the grid field.

Solid SDF hits in the fog pass use stochastic coverage rather than ordinary alpha blending so the renderer keeps the Aetheria transparency/depth contract alive while it grows toward a WebGPU/TAA path.

Next architectural step is to move hard-coded SDF source definitions into a small typed field-source list, then split the monolithic shader into source-field, fog integration, and composition ownership when WebGPU takes over.
sdf_planet_agents: Agent bodies are now field-volume SDF planets, not Three mesh glyphs. DOM captions remain the ID tags and interaction roots; the visible body belongs to the HDR field pass.

Each planet source carries world XY, mass/activity, height, color, and a Self flag. The shader evaluates a local-domain chrome sphere displaced by cheap 4D fBm where xyz is the planet's local domain and w is time.

Agent atmospheres are gassy SDF shells whose thickness and density scale with mass/activity. Self is a solar class: higher displacement, warmer emissive shading, and stronger corona/plasma loop noise.
Keep this path cheap until WebGPU takes over. Per-pixel SDF/fog work can get expensive quickly, so use compact analytic noise and avoid nested source/noise loops in smoke-scale viewports.
aquarium_renderer_architecture: The preferred live Aquarium renderer now uses a WebGPU field overlay for the agent/fog field: a compute pass builds one u32 primitive-membership bitmask per froxel, and the render pass marches pixels while evaluating only primitives named by the current froxel.

Solid and volumetric paths share that froxel primitive mask. While marching a ray, each sample reads the current froxel's bitmask; named primitives are evaluated for both solid SDF hits and atmosphere density. A solid SDF hit shades the solid and terminates the ray.

Diffuse volumetric lighting now belongs to froxel space: a WebGPU compute pass ping-pongs first-order SH coefficients, propagates them through six neighbors, injects studio HDR summary light from the volume edges, and injects local Self emission before the raymarch samples the coefficients.

Fit froxel volumes in depth, not screen x/y. The WebGPU froxel grid should keep canvas-local x/y dimensions aligned to the screen while Three projects the moving grid volume's near/far depth bounds; agent primitives carry projected body depth so z slices avoid fog work outside the grid volume.

Agent solid body size should be consistent in world space across the swarm, not fixed in screen pixels or multiplied by a projection-scale patch. WebGPU should reconstruct camera rays from Three's camera frame and intersect world-space planet SDFs against world-space centers/radii; Self may have solar emission and a larger/warmer atmosphere, but its solid SDF radius and DOM anchoring should follow the same rules as every other celestial body.
The fitted grid/fog volume is the visibility window. Do not let solid planets render outside it; solids and gas should fade at the near/far bounds of the current grid volume.

The visible aquarium field should be the WebGPU marched renderer. Three may provide camera/projection/source rigging, but the screen should be owned by compute/froxel/marching output: heightfield grid surface, fog bank, SDF bodies, and atmospheres.

In the Bevy host, treat the camera target as the Grid center invariant. Clamp it to global XY, derive GridFrame.center from it, derive GridFrame.half_extent from camera distance, and sample/build the heightfield over that moving square so future gravity render targets can align to the same domain. Do not move agent orbit anchors with the camera/Grid frame; those anchors are world-space simulation state.

The Bevy raymarcher is back as a native fullscreen WebGPU pass attached to the camera. The current lean pass is solid-only: the Grid is marched as solid heightfield terrain, agent bodies are solid SDF planets, fog/atmosphere accumulation is removed, and a CPU-built packed froxel bitmask skips empty body tests along each ray.

The Bevy host no longer renders traditional mesh geometry for the visible aquarium world. Grid terrain, body planets, and cursor probes are source data for the fullscreen raymarcher; ECS Transform/CelestialBody entities remain as simulation/cache/audio anchors, and Bevy Text2d captions remain the temporary label surface.

Bevy local lighting now uses a compact first-order spherical-harmonic froxel cache in the raymarch uniform. Self is the only active radiance injector; previous SH coefficients decay and propagate through neighboring froxels each frame, and terrain/planet shading samples that cache instead of procedural fullbright environment light.

The Bevy raymarcher has a first Bruneton-inspired atmosphere slice: camera rays integrate exponential density clinging to the Grid heightfield, clipped and faded by a circular radius mask around the current Grid center, using SH froxel lighting for in-scatter and transmittance over the solid terrain/body path. This is a compact uniform-era pass, not the final compute precompute texture stack.

If Bevy atmosphere shows vertical bands, suspect the SH lighting lattice first. The current mitigation is trilinear SH sampling, a 32x32x12 Grid-space light volume, a softer radial domain fade, and stable per-pixel jitter for terrain/atmosphere ray steps.

Bevy volumetric lighting now runs on the GPU. The generic FullscreenMaterial helper was replaced by a custom render node that dispatches `cs_grid_lighting` before the fullscreen raymarch. Two storage buffers ping-pong first-order SH coefficients in Grid space; the compute pass advects/scatters them, reprojects history through previous Grid center/scale as a 2D XY problem, injects Self radiance, and the fragment pass samples by world point.

Do not enable `bevy/dynamic_linking` in the Windows hotpatch path. Bevy 0.18's `bevy_dylib` can exceed MSVC link.exe's 65,535 object limit and fail with LNK1189; keep Aquarium's `hotpatch` feature on `bevy/hotpatching` without dynamic linking unless the linker strategy changes.

Three loads `public/textures/studio3.hdr` through RGBELoader/PMREM and assigns it to `scene.environment` for PBR lighting. WebGPU field chrome currently matches the studio lighting direction procedurally; direct HDR sampling needs a WebGPU-owned parsed/prefiltered environment texture, not a WebGL PMREM cross-API borrow.

The Three/WebGL layer still owns the moving Aetheria gravity grid, cursor, and fallback rendering. When navigator.gpu exists, Three marks the field as externally rendered and skips the expensive WebGL field-volume pass.

Aetheria-style deferred 2D source fields are live now: sparse PowerPulse/wave splats accumulate into a grid texture, and grid/stardust/fog sample that moving domain. Full Wronski density/light injection, sparse bricks, TAA, and Bruneton atmosphere remain next-stage architecture.

Only introduce sparse brick maps for fields that cannot be cheaply derived at sample time: persistent volumetric memory, authored complex gas, cached lighting, or demand-refined large spaces. Do not brick-map simple agent SDFs just to look serious.
bruneton_atmosphere: Bruneton's atmospheric scattering model is a precomputed light-transport cache, not a per-frame sky raymarch. Runtime shaders query transmittance, scattering, optional single-Mie, and irradiance textures for sky radiance, aerial perspective, and surface lighting.

The pass graph matters: compute transmittance; compute direct irradiance; compute first-order Rayleigh/Mie scattering; then for orders 2..N compute scattering density, indirect irradiance, and multiple scattering deltas before accumulating them into final textures.

Texture domains are the API. Transmittance is keyed by radius and view zenith; irradiance by radius and sun zenith; scattering by radius, view zenith, sun zenith, and view-sun angle packed into a 3D texture. Do not hide domain mapping in magic constants.

Keep physical quantities honest. Bruneton's GLSL uses type-like macros, and the same equations compile as C++ with dimensional types for unit checking. Aquarium shader math should get CPU/reference tests for critical transport and coordinate mapping instead of trusting pretty pixels.

Atmosphere parameters should be explicit: solar irradiance, sun angular radius, bottom/top radii, Rayleigh density/scattering, Mie density/scattering/extinction/phase asymmetry, absorption/ozone, ground albedo, and the sun-angle range worth precomputing.

For Aquarium, split global atmosphere from local fog. Stable horizon-scale sky/aerial-perspective transport belongs in Bruneton-style precomputed or cached fields; local gassy SDFs, cursor wakes, and agent fog stay dynamic stochastic/froxel/raymarch fields lit by those caches.

Color is a contract. Bruneton supports RGB radiance with runtime luminance conversion or slower precomputed luminance from more wavelength samples; start pragmatic in RGB/HDR, but keep the spectral-to-luminance decision explicit if mood/sky color becomes a design surface.
dreams_doctrine: Separate authoring, evaluation, and rendering representations. Dreams kept user-authored sculpt intent as lists of simple SDF edits, evaluated that into surface samples/caches, then rendered painterly splats/flecks; the editable source and visible output did not need to be the same data structure.

Prototype renderers can fail while preserving machinery. Dreams abandoned marching-cubes blobs, polygonalized SDFs, gigavoxel hybrids, fuzzy brick compositing, and refinement renderers, but carried forward useful pieces: SDF edit lists, hierarchical culling, point-cloud surfaces, stochastic LOD, TAA reliance, and artist-friendly gesture flow.

Art direction can invalidate technically impressive truth. Direct SDF/surface renderers exposed too much literal geometry and left little room for the painterly/clay imagination; the shipped splat/fleck style won because it matched creation feel, not because it was the most orthodox renderer.

Use SDFs as an intermediate truth, not necessarily the runtime renderer. Evaluate zero crossings from sculpt edits into dense, even surface point clouds; use the field for collision/tooling/evaluation while rendering a filtered cloud of visible marks.

Cluster point clouds spatially and feed the GPU coherent chunks. Dreams sorted surface samples through Hilbert-like locality, packed clusters of roughly hundreds of points with bounds/normal bounds, compressed point attributes, and built separate clustered mip levels rather than relying on one mutable mesh.

Use stochastic rendering when temporal accumulation is part of the contract. Russian-roulette point counts, stochastic transparency, noisy current frames, and splat disc jitter become acceptable if TAA is designed as a core resolver rather than a final polish filter.

LOD should change density gracefully, not pop representation. Dreams smoothed point-cluster LOD by probabilistically reducing visible points and by using independent point-cloud mips; distant flecks can become larger/looser while close flecks can expand into mini point clouds.

Rasterization is not always the fastest splatter. Compute splatting with atomics can beat quad rasterization for sparse textured splats because it does not pay for transparent texels that will contribute nothing.

Hard product constraints create architecture. Dreams' public pitch was not collage of premade assets: no imported textures, models, or meshes, everything authored on PS4/controller, so the renderer had to serve user creation all the way down.

A reductive tool can beat a complete tool. Dreams supported add/subtract/color lists of SDF edits before ZBrush-like smudge/pull/deform features; that accidental simplicity made QA and artists less intimidated than topology, vertices, UVs, and conventional meshes.

Soft blends and nonlocal edits are enemies of culling. SDF edit evaluators must make soft min/max revert to hard behavior outside finite influence ranges, use interval arithmetic where possible, and choose distance norms that make bounds reliable.

Compute pipelines can become unmaintainable even when mathematically parallel. The Dreams edit-list-to-sparse-field path became dozens of chained compute shaders that were hard to debug on early PS4 hardware; parallelism is not enough if the pass graph becomes a cursed machine room.

Point jitter effects must respect visibility semantics. Dreams' point-cloud depth of field worked because scattered points could still occlude within one depth buffer; naive temporal point jitter for motion blur failed because each time sample wants its own visibility/depth solution.

Painterly lighting can use painterly cheats. Imperfect shadow maps, noisy one-ray-per-pixel AO, dynamic voxelized occlusion, and TAA-resolved stochastic garbage were acceptable because the visual style embraced filtered marks instead of sterile correctness.

Tool feel is an engine requirement. Minimal UI intrusion, gestural sculpting, edit-history/timelapse affordances, and artists using half-built tools shaped Dreams as much as renderer choices; Aquarium should let living interaction grammar steer representation decisions.
compute_and_audio: For realtime audio, keep enough queued samples ahead of playback.
Use GPU or batched generation for expensive spectral work.
Agent voices can be continuous; interface controls should be transient.
Subtractive interface hits start with noise and shape it with resonators.
interaction_design: Progressive disclosure is the core grammar: vibes first, object second, surface third.
Spatial memory matters; put controls near the thing they operate on.
Do not make hidden hit zones that lack visible affordances.
Every animation needs a reason: orient, acknowledge, warn, invite, or delight.

Swarm registry presence is not Epiphany liveness. A registered but non-running member should appear as a sleeping cold body; only heartbeat/running signals justify exploding it into the specialist constellation.

warnings: Calling something diegetic does not make it diegetic.
A panel that is always visible is still chrome, even if it has a nice blur.
Do not let fluid-only ghosts leak UI that DOM does not own.
Do not let cute become illegible when the user actually needs to work.
